title: An automorphism of a reduced finite-type scheme that induces the identity on the underlying topological space acts trivially on coherent modules and is the identity in positive dimension
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section on automorphisms
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that an automorphism f of a reduced finite-type scheme over k fixing every point of the underlying topological space preserves every coherent module, and equals the identity provided every irreducible component has positive dimension. The proof is a cascade of reductions - to irreducible components, to a dense affine open, to a single affine algebra with k infinite or finite - and at each stage a density argument (the union of the V(g-lambda) for lambda in k, or the closed points with prime-to-n degree) forces g = f^sharp(g) and hence the identity (proof lines 6085-6145). H2: several independent reductions and the two field-size cases are the substance; none is written out anywhere else in the span.
